project_specification.project_name: nullius — bind the live LLM providers into the signal agent and the policy-development agent
project_specification.addition_summary: The providers member has live LLM backends (additions_spec_live_providers.xml), but nothing calls them. This addition makes the two LLM roles of docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md section 14.1 real. - The signal agent becomes an LLM author: the agent callable that discovery.NodeExpansion(agent, database_url) already accepts. It builds the C3 prompt from the campaign's complete proposal history, calls the model chosen for the node's role, parses the answer and runs it through the signal-agent gates. - The policy-development agent becomes an LLM reviser: the Reviser that dreaming.revise_policy(..., reviser=) already accepts. - Every live call leaves an authoring record. Once the node row exists, that record is written to the existing provenance stores: the node's agent_model_id pin (203), its agent_sampling (204), the root call's serving provider and its rotation assignment (196 and 197). At the end of a campaign, the depth role's measured cache hit rate is written as well (200). Out of scope: - the campaign driver (planting roots, then the select, expand, evaluate and persist loop); - the depth-model admission and price gates (198, 199, 201, 202), which need pricing data no config carries yet; - batch APIs; - operator wiring of API keys into run.sh or the 1Password templates.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace / stdlib plus workspace members only / SQLite or PostgreSQL via DATABASE_URL / pytest (ruff conventions)
existing_context.test_baseline: Measured 2026-10-05: packages/providers/tests 1221 passed, packages/signal-agent/tests 633 passed, workspace tests/ 1592 passed. All green on main (HEAD a8cf426).
existing_context.conventions:
Follow CLAUDE.md's Build & Test section and its rules: - Only workspace members, under packages/<name>/. - @register builders live only in a member's __init__.py. - Components are read through create_app().get(name), or by direct import within their own member. - A refusal is a typed error that opens with a greppable code word and is defined in the module that raises it. - Tests never reach the network or read a real credential. Model calls in tests go through providers.RecordedProvider, or a live backend with an injected fake transport.
Existing pieces (read, do not change unless a feature says so): - providers: - Request(messages, model, temperature, max_tokens) and Message(role, content). - Completion(content, model, usage: Usage(input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens), finish_reason). - ModelPin(provider, model, version), stored as "p/m/v". - live_provider(pin, env=None, transport=None) -> Provider, require_served(pin, completion), and BudgetedProvider(inner, *, max_input_tokens, max_output_tokens). - The "live-providers" component, whose resolver answers resolve(pin). - AgentSampling(temperature, top_p=1.0, thinking=False, seed=0) and HOSTED_API_CKPT_HASH. - AgentModelPins (component "agent-model-pins"), with persist(node_id, pin) and persist_weights(node_id, ckpt_hash=HOSTED_API_CKPT_HASH, *, sampling). Both need the node row to exist. - FrontierProvider(provider, model), FrontierTier(providers=(FrontierProvider, ...)) and ROOT_TIER_MAX_DEPTH = 1. - rotation_index(campaign_id, node_id, tier) -> int. This is a pure sha256 decision. - RootRotation (component "root-rotation"), with record_root_provider(call, serving, tier, *, now=None). call is RootCall(node_id, campaign_id, depth), and its node row must exist with depth <= 1. A serving provider other than the assigned one raises UnassignedRootProviderError. - DepthCacheRates (component "depth-cache-rates"), with measure(campaign_id, usages, *, now=None). It is write-once per campaign, so the same totals again are accepted and different totals raise CacheRateConflictError. - discovery: - NodeExpansion(agent, database_url) calls agent(NodeWorkspace) with NodeWorkspace(node_id, parent_id, campaign_id, theme_root, depth). - The agent returns one object with .code (non-blank str) and an optional .stated_mechanism (str or None). Extra attributes are ignored. - The child node's id is uuid.uuid5(discovery.EXPANSION_NAMESPACE, str(parent node_id)), and its depth is the parent's depth + 1. - AttemptProvenance(evaluator_hash, snapshot_hash, cost_model_hash, agent_model_id: str, agent_sampling: dict, agent_ckpt_hash) is written onto the node row by record_attempts. - signal-agent: - SignalContract.adopt(source) -> SourceAdoption (.adopted, .problems, .detail, .require()). - PromptGuidanceGate.admit(prompt_parts) -> GuidanceVerdict. The prompt must be named parts, and a flat str is refused. - AntiConvergenceGate: require_in(prompt) checks that the committed clause appears verbatim, and admit(source, held) -> AntiConvergenceVerdict. - MechanismDiagnosis.diagnose(source, complaints=(), ...) -> DiagnosisVerdict. - ProposalHistoryStore: history(campaign_id) -> tuple[PriorProposal(node_id, proposal, code_hash), ...], and persist(node_id, proposal, *, score=None). - dreaming: Reviser = Callable[[str, int, Any], str], meaning (incumbent_source, revision_index, seed) -> source. Its call site is revise_policy(incumbent_source, count, *, seed, reviser=None). - Today signal-agent depends only on the contract member, and dreaming only on its existing members. Neither depends on providers or discovery.

category.name: Authoring Foundation
category.feature: System persists the workspace dependencies the authors need to uv.lock: signal-agent gains the providers and discovery members, and dreaming gains the providers member. - Only workspace members are added, as [tool.uv.sources] workspace = true entries, the same way the existing member dependencies are declared. No third-party package is added. - uv.lock is regenerated with `uv lock`, and `uv sync --all-packages` succeeds. - packages/signal-agent/tests and packages/dreaming/tests stay green. No source file is edited.

System creates an AuthoringConfig from the JSON file named by NULLIUS_AUTHORING_CONFIG with providers.load_authoring_config(env=None), or answers None when the variable is unset. - The file holds root_tier (a list of 1 to 3 "p/m/v" pins with distinct providers), depth (one pin), policy (one pin), temperature (0..1, default 0.7), max_tokens (default 8192), and max_input_tokens and max_output_tokens (the per-pin budget ceilings). - Every pin is parsed with providers.require_agent_model_id. A malformed file, a missing key, a duplicate root provider or an out-of-range value raises AuthoringConfigError (code word authoring_config) naming the key. The file never holds a credential. - The module also defines AuthoringRecord, a frozen dataclass with node_id, campaign_id, depth, role (one of root, depth or policy), pin, sampling (AgentSampling with the config's temperature), usage (the summed Usage of every call the authoring made), served_model and tier (the FrontierTier built from root_tier, for root records). AuthoringRecord.attempt_provenance_terms() answers {agent_model_id, agent_sampling, agent_ckpt_hash: None}, ready for discovery's AttemptProvenance. - providers/__init__.py exports load_authoring_config, AuthoringConfig, AuthoringConfigError and AuthoringRecord in __all__, and changes nothing else.

System creates one budgeted provider per pinned model for authoring calls with providers.AuthoringSession(config, resolve), and provider_for(role, *, campaign_id, node_id) answers (provider, pin). resolve is a callable pin -> Provider, such as the "live-providers" resolver. - role root: the pin is root_tier[rotation_index(campaign_id, node_id, tier)], where tier is the FrontierTier built from root_tier in order. This is the same decision RootRotation records, so the recorder never meets UnassignedRootProviderError. - role depth: the depth pin. role policy: the policy pin. Any other role raises AuthoringConfigError. - Each pin's provider is resolved once per session and wrapped in a BudgetedProvider with the config's ceilings, so every call to that pin in the session draws on one budget. - providers.role_for_depth(child_depth) answers root when child_depth <= ROOT_TIER_MAX_DEPTH, and depth otherwise. - providers/__init__.py exports AuthoringSession and role_for_depth in __all__. Tests use a fake resolve that counts calls.

System persists authoring provenance with providers.record_authoring(record, *, database_url=None, env=None) once the record's node row exists. It also persists a campaign's measured depth cache hit rate with providers.record_campaign_cache_rate(campaign_id, records, *, database_url=None, env=None). - record_authoring persists the pin through AgentModelPins.persist(node_id, pin), and the sampling through persist_weights(node_id, HOSTED_API_CKPT_HASH, sampling=record.sampling). - For a root record it also calls RootRotation.record_root_provider( RootCall(node_id, campaign_id, depth), FrontierProvider(pin.provider, pin.model), record.tier). A depth or policy record writes no root row. - Recording the same record twice is idempotent. A missing node row raises the stores' own NodeNotRecordedError, unchanged. - record_campaign_cache_rate passes the usage of every depth-role record of that campaign to DepthCacheRates.measure(campaign_id, usages), and answers the MeasuredCacheRate. Other campaigns' records and root or policy records are ignored, and repeating the call answers the same row. - providers/__init__.py exports both functions in __all__. Tests use a throwaway SQLite database.

category.name: Signal Agent Author
category.feature: System builds the C3 authoring prompt with signal_agent._authoring_prompt.build_authoring_prompt(workspace, history, *, clause), and it creates named prompt parts that PromptGuidanceGate.admit admits and AntiConvergenceGate.require_in accepts. - The parts are task (the signal ABI `signal(ctx: MarketWindow, seed: int) -> pl.Series`, the node's theme_root and depth, and the required answer format), anti_convergence (the committed clause, verbatim), and history. - history is a sequence of (PriorProposal, ScoreRecord or None) pairs. The part holds every prior node of the campaign in full, in the store's order: its node_id, code_hash, complete proposal text, and its score.json, which is ScoreRecord.to_json(), or null for a node not yet scored. Nothing is summarised, sampled or truncated. - ScoreRecord carries the seven metrics and fail_class only, so the prompt never holds a node's null status. The module never imports or reads the nulloracle member. - The answer format asks for exactly one ```python fenced block holding the signal source, and one line starting "Mechanism:" stating the mechanism. - to_request(parts, *, model, temperature, max_tokens) answers a providers.Request: one system message with the task and anti_convergence parts, and one user message with the history part. - The workspace is duck-typed. It reads campaign_id, theme_root and depth.

System parses a model's answer with signal_agent._authored.parse_authored(text), and it creates a ParsedProposal(code, stated_mechanism, proposal), where proposal is the full raw text. - code is the body of the answer's single ```python fenced block. Zero or several python blocks, or a blank body, raise AuthoredOutputError (code word authored_output), defined in this module. - stated_mechanism is the text after the first line starting "Mechanism:", stripped, or None when no such line exists. - The module imports nothing outside the standard library and the signal_agent package.

System authors a refined signal with signal_agent._llm_author.LLMSignalAuthor(session, *, history_store, contract, anti_convergence, guidance, config, max_retries=1). It is a callable taking a discovery NodeWorkspace, and it creates an AuthoredSignal with code, stated_mechanism, proposal and record. - The child's id is uuid.uuid5(discovery.EXPANSION_NAMESPACE, str(workspace.node_id)) and its depth is workspace.depth + 1. providers.role_for_depth(child depth) picks root or depth, and session.provider_for(role, campaign_id, node_id=child id) picks the model. - It builds the prompt with feature 5 from history_store.history(campaign_id), pairing each PriorProposal with history_store.load(node_id).score. It refuses the prompt before any call when guidance or anti_convergence refuses it. - It calls provider.complete(request), and applies providers.require_served(pin, completion). - The answer is parsed with feature 6 and adopted with contract.adopt(code). It is then checked with anti_convergence.admit(code, held=the history's prior proposals). - When the parse, the adoption or the anti-convergence check fails, it retries up to max_retries times. Each retry appends the assistant answer and a user message naming the defect (the adoption's problems, or the refusal's code word). - After the last failed retry it raises AuthoringRefusedError (code word authoring_refused) naming the last defect. - BudgetExhaustedError and ServedModelMismatchError propagate unchanged, and are never retried. - record is a providers.AuthoringRecord with the child's node_id and depth, the role, the pin, the sampling, the usage summed over every call, the served model and the root tier. - Tests drive it with providers.RecordedProvider or a fake provider, and assert the request text carries every prior proposal verbatim.

System creates a "signal-author" component, registered with @register in signal_agent/__init__.py. Its builder answers an LLMSignalAuthor wired to this member's own components and to a providers.AuthoringSession over the "live-providers" resolver, or None when providers.load_authoring_config() answers None. - The builder reads NULLIUS_AUTHORING_CONFIG, and nothing else. It makes no model call, and reads no API key. - The package exports LLMSignalAuthor, AuthoredSignal, AuthoringRefusedError, parse_authored, ParsedProposal, AuthoredOutputError and build_authoring_prompt in __all__. - Every existing export and component of the package is unchanged. The test builds create_app() with the variable unset (None) and with a config file (an LLMSignalAuthor).

category.name: Policy Development Author
category.feature: System creates a revised exploration policy module through a model with dreaming.llm_reviser.LLMReviser(session, *, config), a callable matching dreaming's Reviser (incumbent_source, revision_index, seed) -> source. - It takes the policy pin from session.provider_for("policy", campaign_id="policy-development", node_id=f"revision-{revision_index}"). - The request carries the incumbent source in full, the revision_index and the seed, with the config's temperature and max_tokens. It asks for exactly one ```python block holding the whole revised module. - It applies require_served, and answers the body of the answer's single python block. - Zero or several blocks raise ReviserOutputError (code word reviser_output), defined in this module. So does an answer identical to the incumbent, naming revision_index. - Each call appends a providers.AuthoringRecord with role policy to LLMReviser.records. - revise_policy(incumbent, count, reviser=LLMReviser(...)) works unchanged. A test passes it with a fake provider.

System creates a "policy-reviser" component, registered with @register in dreaming/__init__.py. Its builder answers an LLMReviser over a providers.AuthoringSession with the "live-providers" resolver, or None when providers.load_authoring_config() answers None. - The builder makes no model call and reads no API key. The package exports LLMReviser and ReviserOutputError in __all__. - Every existing export and component of the package is unchanged. revise_policy's default reviser stays default_reviser.

category.name: Authoring Verification
category.feature: System verifies one LLM-authored refinement end to end, with no network, in tests/e2e/test_llm_authoring_end_to_end.py. - Setup: a campaign with one root node row (depth 0) is seeded in a throwaway SQLite database, together with a prior proposal in the ProposalHistoryStore. - An LLMSignalAuthor is built over a providers.AuthoringSession whose resolve answers providers.RecordedProvider fixtures for the root and depth pins. - discovery.NodeExpansion(author, database_url) expands the root. Its RefinedSignal carries the authored code and stated mechanism. - The attempt is persisted with AttemptProvenance built from record.attempt_provenance_terms(). Then record_authoring(record) is called, and the proposal is stored with ProposalHistoryStore.persist. - The test asserts that the node row carries the pinned agent_model_id and agent_sampling, that the root serving-provider row names the pin's provider, and that the proposal row holds the raw answer. - A second expansion at depth 2 uses the depth pin. record_campaign_cache_rate then persists the campaign's measured rate. - An LLMReviser with a RecordedProvider revises an incumbent through revise_policy. - A refusal path is covered: a fixture answer without a python block, retried once, raises AuthoringRefusedError.

project_specification.integration_points: New modules: - providers._authoring, providers._authoring_session and providers._authoring_store, whose names features 2, 3 and 4 export; - signal_agent._authoring_prompt, signal_agent._authored and signal_agent._llm_author; - dreaming.llm_reviser. New components: "signal-author" (signal-agent) and "policy-reviser" (dreaming). Both answer None unless NULLIUS_AUTHORING_CONFIG names a config file. Features 2, 3 and 4 add exports to providers/__init__.py, and features 10 and 12 are the only edits to the signal-agent and dreaming __init__.py. Feature 1 is the only edit to the manifests and uv.lock. Every new file is committed as an empty stub so its claim resolves. The campaign driver that calls the author and the reviser in a loop is a later spec. Until then, a caller wires them as feature 11 does.
project_specification.constraints: - No test opens a network connection or reads a real credential. Model calls in tests use RecordedProvider fixtures or fake providers, and no API key appears in any file, fixture, log line, exception or repr. - No third-party dependency. Feature 1 adds workspace members only. - Do not edit run.sh, .env.tpl, .env.vst.tpl, .env.example, claw-forge.yaml or claw-forge.local.yaml. - Do not edit the existing modules of discovery, of policy-runtime, or of the providers live backends (_live_http, _anthropic, _openai_compat, _live, _budget, live_check). - The router member and the order path never import providers, signal_agent or dreaming's reviser. There is no model in the order path. - The C3 history is never summarised or truncated. - No authoring module imports or reads the nulloracle member, the null sidecar or any is_null value. The agent sees only ScoreRecord metrics (docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md design principle 2). - Do not edit docs/user-journeys/. - All existing workspace tests (tests/) and the member suites of providers, signal-agent, dreaming and discovery stay green.

implementation_steps.step: Phase 1: workspace dependencies (feature 1), the authoring config (feature 2) and the output parser (feature 6), in parallel.
Phase 2: the session (feature 3), the recorder (feature 4) and the prompt builder (feature 5).
Phase 3: the signal author (feature 7) and the policy reviser (feature 9).
